Blog Warmed routes
AO
Ada Okafor Nov 12, 2026 · 8 min read

A cold route is a store your agent has not bought from in a while. Reaching its checkout means loading the catalogue, finding the item, filling the cart and walking every step of the payment form. On a good day that takes two or three minutes.

A warmed route has already done that walk recently. The session is ready, the form is known, and the purchase takes seconds.

What we keep warm

We watch which stores your agents use and keep those routes ready around the clock. Everything else stays reachable, only slower on the first call. You do not configure any of it; the call is the same either way.

  • The stores your agents bought from in the last week.
  • The stores your customers search most, even before a first purchase.
  • Every route the monitoring shows as degraded, until it recovers.

What it looks like in code

Nothing changes. commerce.buy picks the warm route when there is one and tells you which it took: 

              {`const order = await agentcard.commerce.buy({\n  query: "USB-C charger, 65W",\n  maxPrice: 40,\n});\n\norder.route; // "warm"`}

When a route goes cold

If a store changes its checkout, the route is re-learned within minutes. Until it is, the status table shows the store as degraded and the call falls back to the slower walk. Read more in the docs.

A purchase your agent makes should feel like one a person makes: quick, and finished.
